//: W3 (2026-10 policy): the firearms a player can find at police and army sites, and nowhere else.  Civilians and random NPCs carry none (audit_us_content.py, saigon_random_npcs).  Each is described, never named: the content bible's rule is no trademarks or model names, so the pattern, the cartridge and the mechanism are given and the arsenal and the designation are not.  All of them load dda ammunition.  This one is the rifle the army carried in 2004: the folding-stock version of the stamped-receiver 7.62x39mm assault rifle, as issued to paratroops, vehicle crews and the guard posts.
description: The army's rifle: a stamped steel receiver, a laminated wooden handguard gone dark with sweat, and a steel stock that folds under the receiver so the rifle rides short in a truck or across a guard's chest.  It fires the 7.62x39mm cartridge from a curved thirty-round magazine, one shot at a time or in bursts, and it will keep firing dirty, wet and neglected.  The selector is stiff and loud: everyone near you hears it go from safe to auto.

//: W3: the curved steel magazine of the rifle above.  looks_like the dda magazine of the same pattern, so no new art (D1).
description: A curved magazine of stamped steel with ribbed sides, for the army's folding-stock rifle.  Thirty rounds of 7.62x39mm.  The paint is worn through to bright metal where it has rubbed against a webbing pouch for years.

//: W3: the older semi-automatic carbine the army handed down to the militia, the border posts and the ceremonial guards: a ten-round fixed magazine loaded from stripper clips, and a bayonet that folds back under the barrel (dda's integrated bayonet).
description: A long wooden-stocked carbine in 7.62x39mm, older than the folding-stock rifles and handed down to the militia, the border posts and the honour guards.  It holds ten rounds in a fixed magazine, loaded from the top with a stripper clip or one round at a time, and fires one shot per pull.  A blade bayonet is hinged under the muzzle: swing it forward and it locks, and the carbine becomes a short spear.  Accurate, heavy, and very well kept: someone oiled this one every week.

//: W3: the stripper clip for the carbine; dda's own is named after the rifle, so the mod has its own.
description: A thin strip of grooved steel that holds ten 7.62x39mm rounds, for pushing them all at once into the carbine's fixed magazine.

//: W3: a pump shotgun of the kind the district police, the river police and the bank and port security units held: a plain 12 gauge pump with a short barrel and a five-shell tube.  dda's pump shotguns carry maker names in their variants, so this one is built from the base class.
description: A plain 12 gauge pump shotgun with a short barrel, a black synthetic stock and a five-shell tube under the barrel.  The district police kept a few for the night shift and the port and bank guards had more.  Rack the slide and everyone in the street knows what you are holding.

//: W3: the old side-by-side 12 gauge that border units and rural militia kept in their racks.  Built from the base class for the same reason as the pump.
description: An old double-barreled 12 gauge shotgun with the barrels side by side, a hinged breech and a dark wooden stock rubbed pale at the grip.  Border posts and rural militia kept them in the rack for wild pigs, stray dogs and the occasional smuggler.  Two shots, then break it open and reload.

//: W3: the submachine gun the northern arsenals built in the 1960s from an older Soviet-pattern design, in the 7.62x25mm pistol cartridge, which outlived its war in the armories of the police reserve and the militia.  dda removed its own 7.62x25mm submachine gun (obsoletion_and_migration_0.I), so this one is complete here; its sprite is that gun's.
description: A short, heavy submachine gun with a perforated steel jacket around the barrel, a wire stock that slides forward under the receiver, and a pistol grip.  It fires the 7.62x25mm pistol cartridge from a curved thirty-five-round magazine, fast enough to empty it in a few seconds.  It is older than anyone who was ever issued it, and the police reserve kept a rack of them for emergencies like this one.

//: W3: the curved box magazine of the militia submachine gun.
description: A curved steel box magazine for the militia submachine gun, holding thirty-five 7.62x25mm pistol rounds in two staggered rows.

//: W3: dda's 7.62x39mm descriptions speak of imports and of hunting with surplus rifles in America, and name a rival maker's cartridge; the rounds the army stored in 2004 are described plainly.  Stats are dda's.
description: 7.62x39mm ammunition with a 124gr jacketed, lead core bullet: the intermediate rifle cartridge of half the world's armies, packed in sealed tins of seven hundred.  The brass case can be reloaded.
7.62x39mm ammunition with a 123gr jacketed, hollowpoint bullet, made for hunting medium game.  It opens up on impact instead of passing straight through.

//: W3: the militia submachine gun loads dda's 7.62x25mm, which dda names after the Soviet pistol.  As N4 did for 9x18mm, the rounds and casings the player sees are named after the cartridge alone; stats are dda's.
description: A 7.62x25mm pistol cartridge with a jacketed hollowpoint bullet.  The bottlenecked case drives a light bullet very fast, which made it the round of a generation of pistols and submachine guns in the Eastern Bloc.
An empty casing from a 7.62x25mm round.
An empty casing from a 7.62x25mm round, with its primer removed.
